title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 4th District

context.text: Incumbent William Timmons (R) won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary. Courtney McClain's June 9, 2026 Democratic primary was canceled and she advanced without a primary contest.

candidates.name: William Timmons

summary.text: William Timmons is the incumbent U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 4th District, seeking re-election.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from George Washington University (2006), master's degrees from the University of South Carolina (2009) and New York University (2021), and a law degree from the University of South Carolina (2010).
Owned a small business, worked as a prosecutor in the Thirteenth Circuit Solicitor's Office, and served as a captain and JAG officer in the South Carolina Air National Guard.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (chairman of the Military and Foreign Affairs Subcommittee; also on the Delivering on Government Efficiency Subcommittee) and the Committee on Financial Services (2025-2026 assignments).

candidates.researchNotes: No current-cycle Candidate Connection survey response or campaign-site issue statements were located within the research budget. Key floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Courtney McClain
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced without a primary after the Democratic primary was canceled

summary.text: Courtney McClain is a civil rights advocate running as the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 4th Congressional District. Ballotpedia describes her as the youngest and first Black woman to run for this seat.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of South Carolina, Columbia (2023) and a graduate degree from Howard University (2025).

Worked in Washington, D.C. with the Congressional Black Caucus Foundation and Congressional Black Caucus Institute as an intern and fellow, and has testified before the South Carolina House and Senate on education, reproductive rights, gun violence, voting rights, and criminal justice reform.
Affiliated with the NAACP and Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated.

priorities.text: Tackling the housing crisis, protecting and expanding healthcare access, and fully funding public education.
Says she is passionate about voting rights, education, criminal justice reform, affordable housing, and healthcare.

positions.summary: Lists protecting and expanding healthcare access as one of her three key campaign messages.
